text:
Ottawa's week has been loud in every direction. Nick Cousins took a hit from Jakob Chychrun that one headline called gruesome, was ruled out 7 to 10 days, and the fallout has kept running, down to Cousins unfollowing Chychrun. Tyler Boucher made his NHL debut and scored the winner with his father Brian watching. Shane Pinto scored an overtime winner on his birthday. And Drake Batherson said, per Daily Faceoff, that Sidney Crosby "can have my house" if he ever comes to Ottawa.

Underneath the noise is a good team. The Senators have points in seven straight (5-0-2) with 59% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in that run, and 54% at five on five for the season. Thursday's 6-5 overtime loss to Philadelphia, after leading by three, is the one blemish. Linus Ullmark has been the steadiest thing about them: .940 with 10.3 goals saved above expected, a year after finishing at minus 13.3. William Eklund (ankle) is out until January, and Tim Stützle has slid into his spot beside Dylan Cozens, which is no small upgrade. Our numbers give Ottawa an 88% playoff chance.

The Kings are the mirror image. Their 4-3 shootout win in Toronto, from three goals down, was their best night in a while, but they're 2-3-0 in their last five and sit at 16 points despite outchancing teams (+2.4 expected goal difference, -11 actual). Finishing has cost them about seven goals and their goaltending another 6.6. Artemi Panarin is away for personal reasons and Trevor Moore is out; Kevin Fiala, back nine months after a frightening Olympic injury, is one assist from 300. Drew Doughty's free agency is its own subplot, with Daily Faceoff already asking whether the Kings sell him.

Anton Forsberg starts for Los Angeles. Our numbers like Ottawa, 3.27 expected goals to 2.58, with Stützle at 73% for a point.
headline: Ottawa's loud week meets the unlucky Kings
